headline: Resort Activity and National Park Reservations
reservation: Big Sky Resort requires advanced booking for lift tickets, lessons, and specific summer activities like the Lone Peak Expedition. If planning a day trip to Yellowstone, check the NPS site for vehicle reservation requirements which vary by season and entrance. Lodging in the mountain village is separate from park entry permits.

days.title: Alpine Heights and Forest Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Big Sky Town Center

stops.name: Ousel Falls Park Trail
stops.detail: Walk the well-graded path to a thunderous waterfall; it is an ideal introduction to the local Gallatin National Forest.

stops.name: Lone Mountain Lookout
stops.detail: Utilize the resort lift system to reach high-altitude viewpoints for panoramic vistas of the Madison Range.

days.driving: Allow 30 to 45 minutes for local transfers between the Meadow and Mountain villages.
days.note: Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer; descend from high ridges by midday.

days.title: Gallatin River Canyon
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Meadow Village

stops.name: Gallatin River Pullouts
stops.detail: Observe the river's path through the narrow canyon where 'A River Runs Through It' was filmed.

stops.name: Storm Castle Peak Trailhead
stops.detail: Consider this nearby hike for views of the canyon winding toward Bozeman, checking for seasonal mud closures.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for round-trip travel along US 191; watch for wildlife and heavy truck traffic.
days.note: River levels vary significantly with spring snowmelt; check with local outfitters for safety.

days.title: Yellowstone Gateway Exploration

stops.name: West Yellowstone Grizzly & Wolf Discovery Center
stops.detail: Visit this accredited facility to learn about regional apex predators before heading toward the park.

stops.name: Madison River Valley
stops.detail: Drive into the park's west entrance to view the meadows where elk and bison are frequently spotted.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for the round trip to the West Entrance, plus time for park lines.
days.note: Check the NPS website for road closures; the West Entrance is closed to cars in early winter.

intel.title: Mountain Village Access
intel.text: Paid parking applies at the resort base during winter. Free shuttle services connect the Meadow Village to the mountain to alleviate peak congestion.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Effects
intel.text: Reception is generally good in the town center but drops off immediately in the Gallatin Canyon and high basins. Do not rely on GPS for backcountry trail navigation.

intel.title: Canyon Corridor Services
intel.text: Fuel stations are located in the Meadow Village and West Yellowstone, but not along the 45-mile stretch of US 191 between them. Plan your tank accordingly for day trips.

intel.title: Seasonal Transitions
intel.text: Late May and June are 'mud season' when many high trails are impassable and some businesses close briefly. July through September offers the most stable hiking weather.

intel.title: Wildlife Safety
intel.text: This is active grizzly bear country. Carry bear spray in an accessible holster and know how to use it, even on popular trails like Ousel Falls.

plan.arrival: Fly into BZN, pick up your rental, and stop in Belgrade or Bozeman for mountain supplies. The 60-minute drive to Big Sky is scenic but dark at night.
plan.vehicle: An AWD vehicle with winter tires is strongly recommended from October through May. Check rental policies for towing or off-road use.
plan.goldenHour: The Beehive Basin trailhead offers views of Lone Peak; the best light depends on the angle of the sun and seasonal snow cover.
